title: Farnè 2002 · tactile–auditory extinction
citation: Farnè, A., & Làdavas, E. (2002). Auditory Peripersonal Space in Humans. Journal of Cognitive Neuroscience, 14(7), 1030–1043.
notes: Published study settings are available for inspection. See the source-backed method and remaining execution requirements.

cohort.scope: Subset of Experiment 1 without measured auditory neglect or extinction. Their matched right-rear observations are reused.

published_method.apparatus: White noise from a static left-rear speaker, 45° off the sagittal plane at 20 or 70 cm from the head. The experimenter touches the right lateral neck.

trial_families: Paired left sound and right touch

published_method.response: Use the same four verbal alternatives as Experiment 1. The outcome here is left-sound detection, with left-sound-only trials as the within-block comparison.

stimulus_type.source: MIT Press version of record pp. 1034–1036 and 1041, Experiment 2, Fig. 4 caption

source_provenance.value: MIT Press version of record. Manual contact-triggered white-noise or pure-tone output.
source_provenance.source: Farnè and Làdavas (2002), MIT Press pp. 1040–1041, Methods, Experiment 1

trajectory_count.source: MIT Press version of record pp. 1034–1036 and 1041, Experiment 2, Fig. 4 caption

trajectory_path.source: MIT Press version of record pp. 1034–1036 and 1041, Experiment 2, Fig. 4 caption

stimulus_duration.source: MIT Press version of record pp. 1040–1041, Materials and Procedure
stimulus_duration.gap: No fixed duration or contact-duration distribution. Sound-only contact is on experimenter's thumb.

stimulus_speed.source: MIT Press version of record pp. 1040–1041, Experiment 1, Fig. 1 caption

auditory_conditions.source: MIT Press version of record pp. 1034–1036 and 1041, Experiment 2, Fig. 4 caption

value.match: all speaker positions and sound types

gain_envelope.source: MIT Press version of record pp. 1040–1041, Experiment 1, Fig. 1 caption
gain_envelope.gap: Weighting, exact sound shaping and level tolerances unreported.

value.switch: remote switch and optically isolated circuit

renderer_or_apparatus.source: MIT Press version of record pp. 1040–1041, Materials and Procedure
renderer_or_apparatus.gap: Speaker make/model and component timing unspecified.

trial_rows_families.source: MIT Press version of record pp. 1034–1036 and 1041, Experiment 2, Fig. 4 caption
trial_rows_families.gap: Experiment 2 refers to Experiment 1 for unchanged procedures and lists mirrored families.

condition_intermixing.value: Four event families pseudorandom within a block. Sound identity, quadrant and distance vary across cross-modal blocks.
condition_intermixing.source: MIT Press version of record pp. 1040–1041, Experiment 1, Fig. 1 caption

value.within_block: same pseudorandom order in each condition

blocked_or_random_order.source: MIT Press version of record pp. 1040–1041, Experiment 1, Fig. 1 caption
blocked_or_random_order.gap: Exact pseudorandom sequence and randomization algorithm unavailable.

iti_jitter_policy.source: MIT Press version of record pp. 1040–1041, Experiment 1, Fig. 1 caption
iti_jitter_policy.gap: Verbal warning before stimuli is described for the unimodal control. Exact foreperiod and ITI unreported.

response_window.source: MIT Press version of record pp. 1040–1041, Experiment 1, Fig. 1 caption
response_window.gap: Respond immediately after stimulation, with prompt as needed. Numeric deadline unreported.

value.rule: Report sides of perceived events after stimulation, irrespective of modality. Experimenter prompts if no spontaneous reply.

task_sequence_rules.source: MIT Press version of record pp. 1040–1041, Materials and Procedure

value.delivery: brief light contact by touch-sensitive sensor

tactile_stimulus.source: MIT Press version of record pp. 1034–1036 and 1041, Experiment 2, Fig. 4 caption

value.anchor: sensor contact activates sound and delivers touch

soa_table.source: MIT Press version of record pp. 1040–1041, Materials and Procedure

baseline_strategy.value: Left sound only is the main comparison for acoustic extinction. Right touch only is also a trial family.
baseline_strategy.source: MIT Press version of record pp. 1034–1036 and 1041, Experiment 2, Fig. 4 caption

baseline_timing.source: MIT Press version of record pp. 1040–1041, Experiment 1, Fig. 1 caption
baseline_timing.gap: No audio in the single-touch comparison. No sound-relative delay.

catch_trial_type.value: Neither touch nor sound. Correct report is none.
catch_trial_type.source: MIT Press version of record pp. 1040–1041, Experiment 1, Fig. 1 caption

repetitions_per_tactile_soa_condition.source: MIT Press version of record pp. 1040–1041, Experiment 1, Fig. 1 caption

baseline_count.source: MIT Press version of record pp. 1034–1036, 1041, Fig. 4 and Experiment 2 Methods
baseline_count.gap: Two additional conditions run with Experiment 1; two passes inherited rather than separately enumerated.

catch_count.source: MIT Press version of record pp. 1034–1036 and 1041, Experiment 2, Fig. 4 caption
catch_count.gap: Block composition carried over from Experiment 1.

block_count.source: MIT Press version of record pp. 1034–1036 and 1041, Experiment 2, Fig. 4 caption
block_count.gap: Two mirrored conditions are added alongside Experiment 1. Session count carried over, not independently enumerated.

total_trial_count.source: MIT Press version of record pp. 1034–1036 and 1041, Experiment 2, Fig. 4 caption
total_trial_count.gap: Two new conditions × 40 × two sessions, based on unchanged Experiment 1 procedure. No separate delivered-trial log.

implementation_gaps: The original contact-gated waveform, wideband limits, trial order, touch force, and measured physical onset offsets are unavailable.
The published task requires a contact sensor controlling a calibrated physical loudspeaker, clinician-led manual stimulation of the lateral neck, and coding of four verbal response alternatives.
reference_parameters.planner_scope: The study settings describe the source procedure. The Planner contains no executable trial schedule for this profile.

provenance.source: https://doi.org/10.1162/089892902320474481. MIT Press version of record pp. 1034–1036, 1041, Fig. 4 and Experiment 2 Methods
